questions.question: Define primary treatment. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Define primary treatment. [K] / [CO3]
  • Primary treatment is a physical process designed to remove large suspended solids and grit from
  • wastewater. It involves screening to catch debris, grit removal for inorganic solids, and sedimentation
  • in primary clarifiers, where organic matter settles as sludge and fats/oils are skimmed off the surface.

questions.question: Mention the role of methanogens in anaerobic treatment. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Mention the role of methanogens in anaerobic treatment. [K] / [CO3]
  • Methanogens are anaerobic archaea that play the final role in anaerobic digestion. They convert
  • intermediate products such as acetate, hydrogen, and carbon dioxide into methane (CH₄) and carbon
  • dioxide (CO₂). This process stabilises organic matter and helps in biogas production and the reduction
  • of organic pollution in wastewater.

questions.question: Define aeration tanks of water pollution. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Define aeration tanks for water pollution. [K] / [CO3]
  • An aeration tank is a unit in the activated sludge process of wastewater treatment where air or oxygen
  • is supplied to sewage to promote the growth of aerobic microorganisms. These microorganisms
  • decompose and oxidise organic pollutants, thereby reducing the biochemical oxygen demand (BOD)
  • of the wastewater.

  • growth and soil health. It also reduces the need for chemical fertilisers and improves long-term soil
  • productivity.

questions.question: Discuss the applications and importance of air sanitation techniques in public places, hospitals and industries? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the applications and importance of air sanitation techniques in public places, hospitals
  • and industries? [A] / [CO2]
  • Air sanitation- reduction or elimination of microorganisms present in the air to maintain hygienic and
  • safe environmental conditions.[1] . Importance of Air Sanitation - Maintains a hygienic indoor
  • environment and protects public health. a.Hospitals: Air sanitation prevents hospital-acquired
  • infections in operating theatres and ICUs. b. Microbiology Laboratories: Maintains sterile conditions
  • for microbial culture and research. c. Food Processing Industries: Prevents contamination of food
  • products. d. Pharmaceutical Industries: Ensures a sterile environment for drug production. e. Public
  • Buildings: Used in airports, schools, and offices to improve air quality. [8]

questions.question: Explain the causes, symptoms, transmission, and preventive measures of any two parasitic waterborne diseases. / [CO3] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the causes, symptoms, transmission, and preventive measures of any two parasitic
  • waterborne diseases. [U] / [CO3]
  • a.Cryptosporidiosis, Causative agent: Cryptosporidium parvum (a protozoan parasite). Symptoms:
  • Watery diarrhoea, Abdominal cramps, Nausea and vomiting, Fever and dehydration. Transmission:
  • Infection occurs by ingestion of oocysts through contaminated water or food. It can also spread
  • through the fecal–oral route and contact with infected persons or animals. Preventive measures:
  • Drink safe, properly treated water, maintain good personal hygiene and hand washing, avoid
  • consumption of contaminated food and water, and practice proper sanitation and waste disposal.
  • b.Giardiasis-Causative agent: Giardia lamblia.Symptoms: Diarrhoea (often greasy or foul-smelling),
  • Abdominal cramps and bloating, nausea, fatigue, and weight loss.Transmission: Spread through the
  • fecal–oral route by ingestion of cysts in contaminated water or food. It can also occur through
  • person-to-person contact or poor hygiene. Preventive measures: Drink safe and properly treated or
  • boiled water, maintain good personal hygiene and regular hand washing, ensure proper sanitation
  • and disposal of human waste, and wash fruits and vegetables properly before consumption.
  • [10x1 = 10]
